Management is placeholder ('According to Australian guidelines...') - should specify actual Australian ACS guidelines (aspirin 300mg, clopidogrel 300mg, heparin, GTN, morphine, cardiology review, risk stratification)

suggestions: Replace placeholder patient presentation with realistic case: '62-year-old man, 30-minute history central chest tightness (7/10), radiating to left arm, worse with exertion, partially relieved by rest, previous stable angina on GTN PRN'

Provide explicit expected ECG interpretation: 'Rate 92bpm (tachycardia), regular rhythm, normal axis, ST depression >1mm in lateral leads (V4-V6, I, aVL) consistent with lateral ischaemia, negative troponin = unstable angina'

List specific differentials with reasoning: '1. Unstable angina (likely - ischaemic chest pain, ECG changes, negative troponin). 2. NSTEMI (excluded - troponin negative). 3. Urgent cardiology review for angiography ± PCI within 72 hours (high-risk UA).'
Vary vital signs realistically: 'BP 165/95 mmHg (elevated due to pain/anxiety), HR 98 bpm (tachycardia), RR 18/min (mild tachypnoea), SpO2 97% on room air, Temp 36.8°C, Capillary refill <2sec'
